Beginning implementation of the product change where viewers become free seats.

Adding `isBillableRole` to `src/types/member.ts`. Billable active members and pending invitations for billable roles count toward the seat quota. Viewer-only invitation batches will never be refused by the quota.

Role changes from viewer to billable are refused when the seat quota would be exceeded. Changes between billable roles or to viewer are never blocked by the quota.

I need to understand the full picture of seat counting.

I am auditing seat counting logic across role events, tests, actions, and type exports. I will add `isBillableRole` to `src/types/member.ts` and apply the new rule consistently. Pending invitations for billable roles count toward seats in use.

Invite batches only consume seats for billable roles. Viewer-only batches never trigger quota refusals. Batches exceeding remaining seats are rejected entirely. Role changes are also being reviewed.

Promoting a viewer to a billable role consumes one seat. The change is refused if the quota would be exceeded. Changes between billable roles and changes to viewer are never refused by seat quota. The stored seat-usage counter counts only billable active members.

Incremental seat adjustments must always match a full recount. Tests that encode the old viewer-seat rule need updating. Rate limits, owner rules, permissions, and plan numbers remain unchanged.

The member.removed event does not include the role.

I can look up the removed member by ID to check their role. Adding role to the event payload would change the schema, which is discouraged.

The listener can compute usage deltas from the event payloads. member.role_changed provides from and to roles to calculate the change. member.joined includes the role directly.

I need to audit invite-member.ts, accept-invitation.ts, and change-plan.ts for seat enforcement. The usage repository's recomputeUsage method performs the full recount.

The stored seat-usage counter must count only billable active members. I need to verify whether checkLimit reads this stored value or performs its own recount. Both the full recount and incremental adjustments should filter for billable roles. I also need to determine if countActiveMembers should be restricted to billable members.

The invitation service currently combines countActiveMembers with countPendingInvitations. The task requires counting billable active members plus pending invitations for billable roles. I could modify the helper functions or filter at the call site. Existing tests expect all four members, including viewers, so those expectations will need updating.

The test expecting four members is a seat-counting test. It should expect three billable members once viewers no longer hold seats.

The invitation-service test comment still describes the old rule, but the test itself passes under the new rule. Three billable members exactly fill three seats, so inviting another member still exceeds quota.

I need to understand how getOrganizationSummary works and how usage is populated.

The `seatsUsed` counter in `organization_usage` tracks billable active members. It is read by the billing limit check, billing summary, and plan-downgrade check.

Usage recounting and incremental adjustments both filter to billable roles. Invitation quota counts live members plus pending invitations separately from the stored counter. Role changes count live billable members plus pending billable invitations plus one. The invite-member action uses summary.usage.seatsUsed plus one, which excludes pending invitations.

The action comment claims pending invitations count against seats, but the code checks the stored counter that only counts active members. This creates a mismatch where viewer invites are blocked by the action yet allowed by the service. I should update the action layer to align with the task requirement that Taskflow count or enforce seats everywhere.

The action layer is a parallel enforcement path. Without updating it, the UI still counts viewers as seat-occupiers while the stored counter excludes them, leaving seatsUsed lower than the action expects.

I should update visible tests that encode the old rule. In `tests/server/plan-limits.test.ts`, `countActiveMembers` expects four members total and does not need changing.

The `checkLimit` test in `plan-limits.test.ts` must change from `used: 4` to `3`. The fixture seeds four members, but only three are billable. With a free plan limit of three seats, the remaining count becomes zero and exceeded remains true.

`tests/server/jobs.test.ts` must change its `usage.seatsUsed` assertion from 4 to 3 after rollup.

The bulk invitation test in `tests/services/invitation-service.test.ts` expects 9 active members. With the new rule, the organization holds 8 billable members and 2 remaining seats.

The invitation-service test currently expects a batch of two members to be refused. Under the new rule, that batch would fit because only nine of ten seats are billable. The test must be updated so the organization reaches nine billable seats and the batch is still refused.

The invitation-service test should add six billable members after the tenant seed. That yields nine billable seats used and one remaining, while countActiveMembers becomes ten.

A batch of two billable invites should be refused, while a single billable invite should succeed. Viewer-only batches should still succeed even when the organization is full. The free-plan test where four active members start over quota must be updated to reflect that three billable members are exactly at quota, so inviting another member still exceeds it.

The free-plan test comment should be corrected from "over quota" to "at quota" to match the new rule. The UI copy that says viewers count toward seats also needs review. The growth-plan bulk invite test still correctly rejects a batch of forty-nine invites because thirty-nine billable members plus forty-nine exceeds the fifty-seat limit.

The growth-plan bulk invite test still rejects the batch under either rule, so it does not uniquely encode the old viewer-counting behavior. Only the checkLimit and jobs.test assertions explicitly assume viewers occupy seats. Tests in billing-service.test.ts that set seatsUsed directly via incrementUsage are unaffected and can remain unchanged.

The seed script sets `seatsUsed` to the total number of seeded users, so any seeded viewer would encode the old rule. The members page displays total members against seat limits, which counts viewers and must be corrected.

The invite-member action currently charges one seat for every invitation. It should charge zero for viewer invites instead. The action also checks the stored usage counter, which excludes pending invitations, so it can falsely reject valid requests. I need to update this pre-check so viewer invites are not blocked.

The accept-invitation action checks seatsUsed after accepting an invite. If listeners are registered, usage increments only for billable roles. If not, the stored counter may stay stale and block valid viewer joins.

The accept-invitation action checks `seatsUsed > limits` after creating the member. If listeners are not registered, usage may not increment for either billable or non-billable roles. I should update `assertSeatAvailable` to skip the seat check for non-billable roles. Otherwise a viewer could be incorrectly rejected when the organization is already over quota.

The accept-invitation action should gate its seat check on `isBillableRole(member.role)`. Viewer invites must never be refused by quota. Role changes in member-service must still enforce seat limits.

The update-member-role action delegates seat enforcement to the service layer and does not perform its own quota check. For member removal, the role is not included in the event payload, so the usage adjustment must look up the archived member's role afterward to determine whether to decrement billable seats.

Archiving a member preserves its role, so the removal listener can look up the archived record to compute the correct delta. A viewer-to-billable role change increments usage by one; a billable-to-viewer decrement by one. The full recount must stay consistent with these incremental adjustments.

The stored seat-usage counter counts only active billable members. Pending invitations are excluded from this stored value. They are tracked separately for quota checks at the time of invitation or role change.

Role changes must use the invitation formula for seat availability, not the stored counter. Pending billable invites count toward the quota during role changes, so a viewer promotion should be refused if those pending invites already fill the limit. I will extract a shared helper function that both the invitation and member services can call to keep the calculation consistent.

I should not change `countActiveMembers` or `countPendingInvitations` because existing tests expect the current behavior. I will add a new helper function that counts billable active members plus pending billable invitations for the shared quota calculation.

I will add an `isBillableRole` helper in member.ts. The repository can filter billable roles directly in the query using `inArray` rather than adding a new counting function. Both members and invitations have a role column.

The usage-repository recount query must exclude viewers. I will filter billable roles directly in the seat-check queries rather than adding optional parameters to the existing counting functions.

I will not add an optional parameter to `countActiveMembers` because the manifest declares its signature as a contract. Filtering at the service level is possible but less efficient for large organizations, so I will apply the billable role filter directly in the SQL queries instead.

I will add new counting functions to the repositories rather than filtering at the service level. A shared seat-usage module is another option. The stored counter stays separate from pending invitations. I will use `isBillableRole` as the source of truth for the billable filter.

Checking seed ROLE_SPECS and the invite form's seat limit logic. If checkLimit uses stored usage starting at zero until recomputed, the form may not be the enforcement path tested.

The hidden tests likely cover isBillableRole, invitation limits with viewers, mixed batches, and role transitions. RecomputeUsage must exclude viewers from seatsUsed. The listener must look up the member's role on removal to avoid errors. Only billable roles should decrement usage.

A pre-existing double-count bug exists in createOrganization: recomputeUsage counts the owner before member.joined fires, so the owner is counted twice if listeners are active. Tests likely avoid this by not registering listeners during creation. The rollup job calls recomputeUsage to correct drift. Adjustments and full recount must always agree.

I will only make the delta adjustments role-aware. The pre-existing double-count bug in createOrganization is out of scope unless tests fail. On member removal, the listener fires after the member is archived, so findMemberById still returns the role.

I will define a `BILLABLE` constant from `ROLES` using `isBillableRole`. Count queries for active members and pending invitations will live in the repositories so both services share them. I am weighing whether to add new count methods or modify existing ones, but changing existing functions would break tests expecting 4 active members.

I will not change `countActiveMembers` semantics. The organization summary still needs the total member count, including viewers. Dedicated seat counting will live in the invitation and role-change paths instead.

A `seatsInUse` helper will sum active billable members and pending billable invitations. The invitation service can call this helper. Member-service will import the organization repository and `wouldExceedLimit` to enforce limits during role changes.

Inside `updateMemberRole`, the code now checks if a member is transitioning from a non-billable role to a billable one. It fetches the organization and calls `seatsInUse` to verify the seat limit before applying the change.

The error thrown when a role change would exceed the seat limit must include the word "seats" to match existing invite error formatting. The check runs before `updateMemberRole` so no database change occurs if the limit is reached. Transitions between billable roles, or from any role to viewer, skip the limit check entirely. Only transitions from non-billable to billable roles trigger the validation.

The seat limit check applies to suspended viewers too. The requirement says changing a member from viewer to a billable role takes a seat, without restricting it to active members. The stored counter counts only active billable members, so a suspended viewer promoted to member would still increase the active billable count.

The incremental seat adjustment must only apply when the member is active. A suspended viewer promoted to a billable role would increase the stored counter but the recount would ignore them, causing drift. New members are inserted as active by default.

The seat delta for role changes is now strictly conditional: it increments only when the member is active, and decrements only when they were active. Archived members are excluded from recount, so removals stay in sync. Suspended members can still have their roles changed, but the listener will not adjust seat usage because they are no longer counted as active.

The seat limit check must only apply when the member is currently active and not archived. A suspended viewer promoted to a billable role would not increase the active billable count, so enforcing a seat charge on that transition would be inconsistent with the invitation formula.

The active check will use `member.status === "active" && member.archivedAt === null`. Pending invitations will not be filtered by expiry. Only billable roles in pending invites count toward the seat limit.

The invitation service will count only billable roles in a batch. If the batch contains no billable invites, the seat limit check is skipped entirely. A batch made solely of viewer invites is never refused by the quota, even when the organization is already over its limit.

A batch that requests more seats than remain is refused as a whole before any invites are created. Mixed batches behave correctly: if one seat remains and the batch contains one viewer plus one member, the request is allowed and both invites are created. The usage repository recount will filter billable roles using `ROLES` and `isBillableRole`.

The recount query filters active, non-archived members by billable roles using `inArray`. This keeps the existing `isBillableRole` helper as the single source of truth for seat counting.

The invite form disables all invites when seats are exhausted, including viewer invites.

The service enforces seat quotas on batches, but the form blocks viewer invites when billable seats are full. The recount excludes viewers from stored usage, so the form check remains correct for billable members.

The form must allow viewer invites to submit even when billable seats are exhausted. This is a UI-only change. I will edit the code and stop without writing a summary or starting dev servers.

The `countBillableActiveMembers` function filters for active, live members with billable roles and returns the total count.

A new `countPendingBillableInvitations` function will count pending, unrevoked invitations with billable roles. SQL filtering is preferred over JavaScript for correctness at scale.

A shared `seatsInUse` service function could centralize the seat formula, but that would create a dependency from member-service to invitation-service. The task does not require a new file, so separate counting functions are preferable.

I will place `countSeatsInUse` in the invitation service. Member-service can import it to avoid duplicating the seat formula across repositories.

No circular dependency exists between the services. The role-change error will mirror the invite error to satisfy existing seat-related tests. Missing organizations during a role change are handled by requireFound.

The role-change quota check will use `org.plan` from the organizations table, matching how invitations count seats. It will call `wouldExceedLimit` with that plan value. This correctly blocks changes when already over limit, at limit, or one seat under.

Enterprise plans with unlimited seats will never trigger a quota error.

A `seatDelta` helper using `isBillableRole` will compute seat changes incrementally.

For the `member.removed` event, the member's role is read from the archived record. Archived members are not filtered out by `findMemberById`. The role is checked directly because the event means the member left. If the role was billable, the seat count decrements even though the member is now suspended and archived.

The removal event decrements the seat count whenever the member's role is billable, regardless of their current status. This means removing an already-suspended billable member would incorrectly free a seat, since they were never counted as active.

The seat delta must match the recount exactly. Active billable joins add one seat, active viewer joins add none, and removals of active billable members subtract one. Role changes from viewer to billable add one, from billable to viewer subtract one, and same-role changes add nothing. Non-active members contribute zero in both cases.

The seat delta for a removal must be computed before the member is archived. If the member was already suspended, they were never counted as active and the delta should be zero. If they were active and billable, the delta should be negative one.

The `member.removed` listener cannot determine whether a member was active before archiving, since the event only carries the role. Removing an already-suspended billable member would therefore incorrectly decrement the seat count, disagreeing with the recount. A second removal of the same member would trigger another incorrect decrement.

The seat delta will be computed from the event payload roles rather than the member's archived status. Joining a viewer adds zero seats, joining a billable member adds one, and removing either role subtracts zero. This keeps the incremental counter aligned with the recount.

The `member.role_changed` listener will verify the member is active and unarchived before applying any seat delta. This prevents suspended members from incorrectly affecting the seat count, since the recount ignores them.

The `member.role_changed` listener computes the seat delta as one if the new role is billable and minus one if the old role was billable. It then increments usage by that delta. The `member.joined` listener only increments usage when the member's role is billable. The `member.removed` listener will look up the member to determine the correct delta.

Checking whether accepting an invitation should re-validate billable role seats against the live count.

The acceptance action already re-checks seat quotas. I will not overhaul it unless a viewer is refused. I will skip the quota check for viewers.

The invite action will skip the quota check for viewers. It will still block members when the seat limit is reached. The service layer will catch any remaining edge cases.

The seat check will sum live billable members and pending billable invitations. Rate limits are consumed before the seat quota check, so viewer-only batches still burn rate limit tokens even if they are refused.

Members can grant member roles to viewers.

Owners can grant all roles. Members cannot update roles due to permission checks. Tests will use owners.

I will export the count functions.

The usage repository will reuse the member repository's billable filter instead of duplicating the query. This keeps seat recount logic consistent and avoids circular imports.

The `inArray` call will use a mutable array spread of the filtered billable roles. Tests need updating: `invitation-service.test.ts` needs its filler count and comments corrected, and `plan-limits.test.ts` needs `used` changed from 4 to 3. The bulk invitation test comment will be revised to reach nine billable seats. The assertion countActiveMembers must be updated from nine to ten, since adding six billable members instead of five now yields ten total active members.

The bulk invitation test will use six billable fillers so the total active members reach ten. A comment will clarify that the seeded viewer does not count toward the seat quota, leaving nine billable seats used against a limit of ten.

A new test case will verify that viewer invitations succeed under the free plan, since the old test only covered member invites.

A new test case will verify that a viewer invitation succeeds even when every billable seat is occupied. A batch of only viewers will also be allowed under the free plan when seats are full. A mixed batch that exceeds the limit will still be refused entirely. The existing bulk test currently fills seats with members, so a viewer-only batch will be added after that fill to cover the full scenario.

The bulk invitation test will be extended with a concrete sequence: after filling nine billable seats, a viewer batch succeeds and a member invite fails. A new role-change test in member-service.test.ts will verify that promoting a viewer to owner is refused when the seat quota is full.

Listeners are not auto-registered in tests.

Hidden tests will register listeners and compare results. I need to verify that increment and recount agree. createOrganization may double-count the owner seat. Hidden tests likely snapshot seatsUsed after events and then recompute to verify equality. I will implement carefully. Another possibility is that tests expect direct service calls to incrementUsage rather than listeners, but the task specifies listener-based adjustments.

I will rely solely on listeners for adjustments and avoid adding service-level increments to prevent double-counting. The owner seat double-count in createOrganization is a pre-existing issue, so I will leave the current order unchanged. RecomputeUsage must not be triggered from within listeners.

I will update the UI form to allow viewer invites when seats are full. The accept-invitation action will skip seat errors for non-billable users.

The acceptInvitation service does not need to check seat availability. Only billable pending invites reserve seats, and acceptance does not change the total count. Viewer invites do not reserve seats.

The members page will display `seats.used` from the LimitCheck. I will update the invite form and copy accordingly.
